terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, deponent; with ut and the subjunctive, or ad and the accusative
terms.comment: In poetry also with an infinitive: hortāturque sequī (Ov. Met. 8.215).

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, deponent; with ad and the accusative, or ut and the subjunctive
evidence: Cic. Rab. Perd. 1 (Lewis & Short): mē meae vītae cōnsuētūdō ad C. Rabīrium dēfendendum est adhortāta
Caes. BG 1.25 (Lewis & Short): cohortātus suōs proelium commīsit
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to animate or encourage by forcible language … esp., of the general before a battle”.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 9.14.7 (Lewis & Short): hortātiō nōn est necessāria
Cic. Arch. 1: hujus hortātū praeceptīsque (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In classical prose only in the ablative singular (Lewis & Short): hortātū meō, at my urging.

terms.register: not before Augustus: Ov., Liv. (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: velut āles, ab altō quae teneram prōlem prōdūxit in āera nīdō, hortāturque sequī
phrases.english: like a bird that has led her tender young out of the high nest into the air, and urges them to follow

phrases.latin: sī quidem et rēmigem cantus hortātur
phrases.english: for song spurs on even the rower

phrases.latin: Hortātus est mē ut Latīnē loquerer.
phrases.english: He encouraged me to speak Latin.
